Title: Diagnosis of test `testEncodingInputStream`

Details:
The test `testEncodingInputStream` iterates over some test cases and compares the expected encoding of archives with the encoding detected by reading an archive input stream. It uses the utility method `getInputStreamFor` to obtain an `ArchiveInputStream` for a specific archive format type and test file.

From the investigation, `getInputStreamFor` calls `ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(String, InputStream)`, passing the archive type and an input stream to the archive file. This method creates a specific `ArchiveInputStream` subclass based on the `archiverName` which is the archive type string.

The `createArchiveInputStream` method selects the implementation based on the type and optionally passes an encoding string (`entryEncoding`) if it is set. For example, for ZIP format it returns a `ZipArchiveInputStream` either with or without encoding based on `entryEncoding`.

Looking deeper, `ZipArchiveInputStream` constructors initialize internal fields related to encoding, particularly calling `ZipEncodingHelper.getZipEncoding(encoding)` to handle the encoding. Similar patterns exist for other archive types, e.g. `TarArchiveInputStream` also takes encoding and sets `zipEncoding` based on it.

The failure could occur if the passed `entryEncoding` is not properly set or handled, resulting in incorrect encoding detection compared to the expected one in tests. Alternatively, encoding might not be properly propagated or interpreted in some of these `ArchiveInputStream` subclasses, causing discrepancies.

In sum, the root cause relates to how encoding is handled or propagated from `ArchiveStreamFactory` to the specific `ArchiveInputStream` subclass (e.g., Zip, Tar), affecting how the encoding is detected and returned by `getField(ais, test.fieldName)` in the test.

Next, inspecting how `entryEncoding` is set or defaulted in `ArchiveStreamFactory` and how each archive input stream uses it would be productive to identify the exact encoding-related bug.

Classes/methods to investigate or fix:
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(String, InputStream)
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveInputStream.ZipArchiveInputStream(InputStream, String)
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.TarArchiveInputStream(InputStream, String)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.ArchiveStreamFactory.createArchiveInputStream(java.lang.String,java.io.InputStream)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveInputStream.ZipArchiveInputStream(java.io.InputStream,java.lang.String)
org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.tar.TarArchiveInputStream.TarArchiveInputStream(java.io.InputStream,java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
